key_insight: Foundation ML interatomic potentials can capture simple and some directional low-temperature order in correlated perovskite oxides, but they still fail for purely local spin-state transitions.
engineering_relevance: This matters for screening and simulating perovskite materials because it shows where MLIPs can replace DFT reliably and where correlated-electron physics still needs specialized treatment.
method: Tested three foundation MLIPs on LaMnO3, LaCoO3, and NdNiO3 without system-specific training.
Ran molecular dynamics for 1 ns on 80- and 160-atom supercells over 50–300 K.
Compared predicted low-temperature order across scalar, vector, and on-site classes of correlated behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful capture of NdNiO3 scalar order and LaMnO3 bond-length magnitude, but not the symmetry of the long-bond axis or the LaCoO3 spin crossover.
watch_item: Present-day foundation MLIPs may miss local multiplet/spin-state transitions even when they reproduce structural trends, so validation against correlated-electron observables is essential.
paper_title: Bond, orbital and spin order in d4/d6/d7 perovskite oxides: successes and limitations of foundation interatomic potentials
